requirements.evidence: Default map and range fallback are covered: Queue::DEFAULT_PREFIX_MAP and defaultPrefixFor (app/Models/Queue.php:133-153). prefixForPriority lets a custom entry win (Queue.php:158-167). The saving hook normalizes [] to null and validates canonical keys, A-Z values and unique effective prefixes, including the {"0":"E"} case (Queue.php:174-242). There is an array cast (Queue.php:251). UpdateQueue takes priorityPrefixMap with null/[]/validate semantics and returns ValidationException on 'priority_prefix_map' before it mutates anything (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:81-98). IssueTicket reads the clock once into $now/$issueDate (IssueTicket.php:41-44, 56-57). nextCode filters by issue_date and prefix and skips malformed codes (app/Models/Ticket.php:309-326). The factory aligns issue_date with issued_at and allocates by priority and day (TicketFactory.php:372-406). The migration adds the column, backfills DATE(issued_at), makes it NOT NULL, swaps the unique index and has a down(). Docs and the CHANGELOG are updated. Small gaps: nextCode still defaults the prefix to legacy 'A' when none is passed (Ticket.php:300), and the hard-coded SQLite rebuild fallback could drop columns or misname indexes.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes stay in UpdateQueue/IssueTicket. Authorization is unchanged (Gate authorize 'update'). The #[Fillable] list is unchanged, so the map is not mass-assignable. The migration has a down(). docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md and CHANGELOG.md are updated, and PHPDoc is refreshed on nextCode and the factory. One deviation: the migration contains a hand-written raw-SQL table rebuild and an ALTER TABLE MODIFY fallback (migration lines 446-517), which goes beyond a generated schema edit.

security.evidence: The map is excluded from #[Fillable] (Queue.php:122) and can only be changed through UpdateQueue, which authorizes first (UpdateQueue.php:79). The model validates input on every save (Queue.php:223-241). No UI or Livewire surface was added and no unescaped output was introduced.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/TicketCodePrefixTest.php covers: default and range prefixes; custom map precedence; invalid maps (foo, -1, 010, xx, n, AB, duplicate N, {0:E}); empty map stored as null; independent per-prefix sequences with a daily restart; legacy A001 ignored; gaps not reused; factory day/priority/explicit code; UpdateQueue set/unchanged/clear/invalid leaves the queue unchanged. Existing IssueTicket tests were updated from A to N without being weakened. Missing: the ValidationException key 'priority_prefix_map' is not asserted, there is no N001 -> N-X -> N002 case in the new file (it is covered in IssueTicketTest), the factory priority test only checks toStartWith('P'), there is no non-owner test for the map parameter, and Carbon::setTestNow is reset inline rather than in afterEach.

simplicity.evidence: The core logic is lean. The extra parts are speculative: nextCode now accepts int|Queue and string|CarbonInterface|DateTimeInterface|null with a match-based parser (Ticket.php:297-307), but every caller passes an int and a Y-m-d string. The migration wraps change() in a catch(Throwable) with a 30-line hard-coded SQLite table rebuild plus a raw MySQL ALTER fallback (migration:449-517). validatePriorityPrefixMap repeats the null/[] early returns that the saving hook already handles.

readability.evidence: Names are clear and comments explain the reasoning (IssueTicket.php:39-40, Ticket.php:278-292). The awkward $queueIdOrQueue parameter and the silent legacy 'A' default make nextCode harder to reason about. The migration's fallback paths add cognitive load.

scope.evidence: Nearly everything serves the task. The unrequested widening of the nextCode signature (Queue instance, DateTime types) and the SQLite table-rebuild machinery go beyond what was asked.

issues.explanation: change() is wrapped in catch(Throwable) with a hard-coded SQLite rebuild of the tickets table. If it ever runs, any column not listed is silently dropped and the indexes get 'tickets_rebuild_*' names. Native change() already works on supported Laravel versions, so this fallback is speculative and risky.
nextCode() still defaults the prefix to legacy 'A' when none is passed, so any caller that omits it keeps producing old-style A codes instead of the new default N.
The signature is widened to int|Queue and multiple date types with a match parser, but no caller needs that.
The invalid-map test only asserts ValidationException. It does not check that the error key is 'priority_prefix_map', and there is no test of the map parameter with a non-owner actor.

Carbon::setTestNow() is reset at the end of each test body rather than in afterEach, so a failing assertion leaks the frozen clock into later tests. The factory priority test asserts only toStartWith('P').
validatePriorityPrefixMap repeats the null and [] early returns that the saving hook already handles.

review.summary: The change implements priority-based prefixes, the per-queue validated custom map managed through UpdateQueue, daily per-prefix sequencing with issue_date, single-clock issuance, factory alignment and doc updates, and its tests cover most requirements. I would approve it with nits; the main concerns are speculative complexity (a hard-coded SQLite table rebuild in the migration and a widened nextCode signature), the leftover legacy 'A' default prefix, and some gaps in the error-key and authorization tests.
